questions.q: A water drop of diameter $2$ cm is broken into $64$ equal droplets. The surface tension of water is $0 . 075Nm^{- 1}$. In this process the gain in surface energy will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$By conserving the total volume& $\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 64 \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right)⇒ R = 4r$

Change in surface energy is

$\Delta U = T \times \Delta A$,~$= T \left[64 \times4\pir^{2} - 4\piR^{2}\right]$

$= 4\$piTR^{2}\left[$64 $\times $\dfrac{1}{16} -1\right] = 12 \times3 . 14 \times0 . 075 $\times {10}^{- 4}

$\approx2 . 8 $\times {10}^{- 4}$J$

$

questions.q: A solid sphere, of radius R acquires a terminal velocity ${v}_{1}$ when falling (due to gravity) through a viscous fluid having a coefficient of viscosity $η .$ The sphere is broken into 27 identical solid spheres. If each of these spheres acquires a terminal velocity, ${v}_{2},$ when falling through the same fluid, the ratio  \left(\dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}}\right)$ equals:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If $R$ is the radius of initial drop and $r$ is the radius of new drop, then
$\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 27 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{3}$
Terminal velocity,

~ ~ ~ ~ ~${v}_{T} ∝ r^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{v}_{1}}{{v}_{2}} = \dfrac{R^{2}}{{\left(\dfrac{R}{3}\right)}^{2}} = 9$

questions.q: The height of liquid column raised in a capillary tube of certain radius when dipped in liquid $A$ vertically is, $5$ cm. If the tube is dipped in a similar manner in another liquid $B$ of surface tension and density double the values of liquid $A$, the height of liquid column raised in liquid B would be ______ $m$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The height $h$ through which a liquid will rise in a capillary tube of radius $r$ is given by,

$h = \dfrac{2Tcos\theta}{rρg} ∝ \dfrac{T}{ρ} ∝ \dfrac{2T}{2ρ}$

As we can see in both cases, value of height will remain same. Therefore,

$h^{'} = h = 5cm = 0 . 05m$

questions.q: When two soap bubbles of radii $a$ and $b( b > a )$ coalesce, the radius of curvature of common surface is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Excess pressure at common surface is given by

${P}_{ex} = 4T\left(\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b}\right) = \dfrac{4T}{r}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b}$

$r = \dfrac{ab}{b - a}$

questions.q: A small spherical droplet of density $d$ is floating exactly half immersed in a liquid of density $ρ$ and surface tension $T .$ The radius of the droplet is (take note that the surface tension applies an upward force on the droplet):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dVg = p \left(\dfrac{V}{2}\right)$g + T \left($2\pir\right)$
$⇒ d . $\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}$g = p . $\dfrac{2}{3}\pir^{3}$g + 2\pirT$
$⇒ $\ddfrac{2}{3}r^{2}g\left(2d - p\right) = 2T$
$⇒ r = \sqrt{\dfrac{3T}{\left(2d - p\right)g}}

questions.q: A big drop is formed by coalescing $1000$ small droplets of water. The surface energy will become :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Lets say radius of small droplets is $r$ and that of big drop is $R$. Total volume of the drops will remains unchanged. Therefore,

$\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 1000 \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right)

$⇒ R = 10r$

Now, initial surface energy is, ${U}_{i} = 1000 \left(4\pir^{2}S\right)$ and the final surface energy is,

${U}_{f} = 4\piR^{2}S$

$= 100 \left(4\pir^{2}S\right)$

Clearly, ${U}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{10}{U}_{i}.$

$

questions.q: A drop of liquid of density $ρ$~is floating half immersed in a liquid of density $\sigma$~and surface tension $7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}N{cm}^{- 1}$. The radius of drop in $cm$~will be : (Take : $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Balancing the forces on drop&

Buoyant force& $+$~surface tension~$= mg$

$\sigma\dfrac{V}{2}g + 2\piRT = ρVg$

$2\piRT = \left(2ρ - \sigma\right)2 \cdot $\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$g; \left[\text{As}V = $\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}\right]

$⇒ R^{3} = $\dfrac{3T}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)g}$⇒ R = $\sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 2}N - m^{- 1}}{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right) \times 10}}

$R = $\dfrac{3}{20\sqrt{\left(2ρ - \sigma\right)}}$m = $\dfrac{15}{2ρ - \sigma}$cm$

questions.q: Surface tension of a soap bubble is $2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 2}Nm^{- 1}$ . Work done to increase the radius of soap bubble from $3 . 5cm$ to $7$ cm will be : [Take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,

Work done $=$~change in surface energy of soap bubble

Therefore,

Work done $= 2T \lleft(4\pi{r}_{2}^{2} --4\pi{r}_{1}^{2}\right)

$= 8\piT \left({r}_{2}^{2} - {r}_{1}^{2}\right)$

$= 8 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times0 . $02 \left({7}^{2} -$3 . {5}^{2}\right)$\times {10}^{- 4}$J$

$= 18 . 48 $\times {10}^{- 4}$J$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : When a capillary tube is dipped into a liquid, the liquid neither rises nor falls in the capillary. The contact angle may be $0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$.
Statement II : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capillary rise
$\mathrm{h}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~T} \cos \theta}{\rho \mathrm{gr}} \text {; }$
If $\theta=0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ then rise is non-zero
$\therefore$ Statement-1 is incorrect.

questions.q: Two spherical soap bubbles of radii ${r}_{1}$ and ${r}_{2}$ in vacuum combine under isothermal conditions. The resulting bubble has a radius equal to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Excess of pressure, inside the first bubble
$p_1=\frac{4 T}{r_1}$
Similarly, $\quad p_2=\frac{4 T}{r_2}$
Let the radius of the large bubble be $R$.
Then, excess of pressure inside the large bubble,
$p=\frac{4 T}{R}$
Under isothermal condition, temperature remains constant.
So, $\quad P V=p_1 V_1+p_2 V_2\frac{4 T}{R}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3\right)=\frac{4 T}{r_1}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3\right)+\frac{4 T}{r_2}\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3\right)R^2=r_1^2+r_2^2\Rightarrow \quad R=\sqrt{r_1^2+r_2^2}$

questions.q: Two water drops each of radius 'r' coalesce to from a bigger drop. If ' T ' is the surface tension, the surface energy released in this process is :

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 2 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{R}^3=\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}=2^{1 / 3} \mathrm{R} \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{i}}=2 \times 4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T} \\ & \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{f}}=4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2 \mathrm{~T}=4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T} 2^{2 / 3} \\ & \therefore \text { Heat lost }=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{f}}=4 \pi \mathrm{R}^2 \mathrm{~T}\left[2-2^{2 / 3}\right]\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is thrice the excess pressure inside a second soap bubble. The ratio between the volume of the first and the second bubble is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_0=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1} \qquad \quad \quad \quad\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_0=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_0=3\left(\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_0\right) \\ & \frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_1}=3 \frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{r}_2} \\ & \mathrm{r}_2=3 \mathrm{r}_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{V}_1}{\mathrm{~V}_2}=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}_1^3}{\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}_2^3}=\frac{1}{27}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A mercury drop of radius ${10}^{– 3}m$ is broken into $125$ equal size droplets. Surface tension of mercury is $0 . 45Nm^{– 1}$ . The gain in surface energy is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$

As the volume of the mercury will remain same, therefore

$\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 125\left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right) ⇒ R = 5r$

Now, increase in surface energy

$∆ U = 125 \times \left(S \times4\pir^{2}\right) - \left($S \times4\piR^{2}\right)$

~$= 0 . 45 $\$times4\pi \times \left({10}^{- 3}\right)2 \left[\dfrac{125}{25} -$1\right]$

$= 4 $\times$0 . 45 $\times4\pi \times {10}^{- 6}

$= 2 . 26 $\times {10}^{- 5}$J$

$

questions.q: The ratio of surface tensions of mercury and water is given to be $7.5$, while the ratio of their densities is $13.6$.~Their contact angles, with glass, are close to $135 °$ and $0 °$, respectively. If it is observed that mercury gets depressed by an amount $h$ in a capillary tube of radius ${r}_{1}$, while water rises by the same amount $h$ in a capillary tube of radius ${r}_{2}$, then~the ratio~$\dfrac{r1}{r2}$& is close to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$| {h}_{Hg} | = | {h}_{water} |$

$\dfrac{2{S}_{1}cos{θ}_{1}}{{ρ}_{1}{r}_{1}g} = \dfrac{2{S}_{2}cos{θ}_{2}}{{ρ}_{2}{r}_{2}g}$

Therefore, the ratio of the radii of the respective tubes is,

$\dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{ρ2}{ρ1} \times \dfrac{{S}_{1}cos{θ}_{1}}{{S}_{2}cos{θ}_{2}}$

$\dfrac{r1}{r2} = \dfrac{1}{13.6} \times 7.5 \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{r1}{r2} \approx \dfrac{2}{5}$

questions.q: A large number of water drops, each of radius $r$, combine to have a drop of radius $R$. If the surface tension is $T$ and mechanical equivalent of heat is $J$, the rise in heat energy per unit volume will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$n \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$

$∴ n^{1 / 3}r = R$

$∴$ Total change in surface energy

$= \left(n \left($4\pir^{2}\right) - 4\piR^{2}\right)T$

$⇒ 4\piT\left(nr^{2} - R^{2}\right)$

$∴$ Heat energy

$= $\dfrac{4\piT\left(nr^{2} - R^{2}\right)}{J \times \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}} = \dfrac{3T}{J}\$left(\dfrac{nr^{2}}{R3} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)

Put $nr^{3} = R^{3}$

$∴ $\dfrac{3T}{J} \left(\dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)

$$

questions.q: Consider a water tank as shown in the figure.& It's cross-sectional area is $0 . 4m^{2}$. The tank has~an opening $B$ near the bottom whose cross-section area is $1{cm}^{2}$. A load of $24$ kg is applied on the water at the top when the height of the water level is $40$ cm above the bottom, the~velocity of water coming out the opening $B$ is $vms^{- 1}$. The value of $v$, to the nearest integer,~is~___ .[Take the value of $g$ to be $10{ms}^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$m = 24kg$

$A = 0 . 4m^{2}$

$a = 1{cm}^{2}$

$H = 40cm$

Using Bernoulli's equation,~

$⇒ \left({P}_{0} + \dfrac{mg}{A}\right) + ρgH + \dfrac{1}{2}P{v}_{1}^{2}$

$= {P}_{0} + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒$ Neglecting ${v}_{1}$

$⇒ v = $\sqrt{2gH + \dfrac{2mg}{Aρ}}

$⇒ v = $\sqrt{8 + 1 . 2}

$⇒ v = 3 . 033ms^{- 1}$

$⇒ v ≃ 3ms^{- 1}

$

questions.q: A spherical soap bubble of radius $3$ cm is formed inside another spherical soap bubble of radius $6$ cm. If the internal pressure of the smaller bubble of radius $3$ cm in the above system is equal to the internal pressure of the another single soap bubble of radius $r$ cm. The value of $r$ is _____
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure inside a bubble is given by,& ${P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{r}$.

Pressure inside the bubble of smaller radius will be,~

${P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \left[ \left({P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{6}\right) + \dfrac{4T}{3}\right]

Pressure inside the bubble with radius~$r$,~${P}_{0} + $\dfrac{4T}{r}

Now,

$⇒ {P}_{0} + $\dfrac{4T}{6} + \dfrac{4T}{3} = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{4T}{r}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{r} = \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3}

$⇒ r = 2cm$

$

questions.q:
A spherical ball of radius $1$ mm~and density $10 . 5g{cc}^{- 1}$ is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity $9 . 8$ poise and density $1 . 5g{cc}^{- 1}$. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is~$3696 \times {10}^{- x}N$. The value of $x$ is

(Given,~$g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}\text{and}\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity i.e., terminal velocity is,

& ${F}_{v} = \left(mg - {F}_{B}\right) \left(\text{As},$a = 0\right)$

Here,~${F}_{B}$~is buoyant force.

$⇒ {F}_{v} = V{ρ}_{b}g - V{ρ}_{g}g = $Vg \left({ρ}_{b} - {ρ}_{g}\right) = $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left({10}^{- 3}\right)$3 \times9 . 8\left[ \left($10 . 5 - 1 . 5\$right)\times {10}^{3}\right] \approx$3696 $\times {10}^{- 7}$N$

Thus,~$x = 7$.

questions.q: A thin transparent film with refractive index 1.4 , is held on circular ring of radius 1.8 cm . The fluid in the film evaporates such that transmission through the film at wavelength 560 nm goes to a minimum every 12 seconds. Assuming that the film is flat on its two sides, the rate of evaporation is ____ $\pi \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a thin film interference, a fringe for transmission is formed.
When
$2 \mu x=n \lambda\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{d x}{d t}=\left(\frac{d n}{d t}\right) \frac{\lambda}{2 \mu} \\ & =\left(\frac{1}{12}\right) \frac{560 \times 10^{-9}}{2 \times 1.4}=\frac{5}{3} \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & V=\text { Volume of film }=\pi R^2 x \\ & \frac{d V}{d t}=\pi R^2 \frac{d x}{d t} \\ & =\pi\left(1.8 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \frac{5}{3} \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s} \\ & =54 \pi \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~m}^3 / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$
